page: Amazon Web Services hpc8a.96xlarge is a high performance computing instance driven by 192 dedicated physical cores across an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R45 processor, running up to 4.5 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. It provides 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory rated at 6 GHz, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core, managed via the Nitro hypervisor architecture with support for AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16.

Network infrastructure delivers a baseline bandwidth of 300 Gbps, catering to tightly coupled multi-node HPC tasks. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, requiring remote EBS attachments or distributed network filesystems for data persistence. Benchmark outputs position this profile in the top tier across raw multi-core compute, extensive memory read/write throughput, and software compilation benchmarks.

Single-core performance registers in the top tier on both Geekbench and stress-ng suites, complemented by substantial parallel bandwidth exceeding 1000 GB/sec for large-block memory reads. While large-scale LLM prompt processing captures top-tier throughput via instruction-level vectorization, generative token emission rates remain within the average tier due to the lack of discrete GPU hardware.

Cost efficiency scales favorably for massive parallel workloads, scientific simulations, ray tracing, and high-throughput computational batch jobs where physical core isolation and high memory frequencies offset the reliance on network storage volumes.
description: Amazon Web Services hpc8a.96xlarge is a dedicated high performance computing instance built on 192 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor running at 4.5 GHz with a 1:1 core-to-thread topology. Equipped with 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory (6 GHz) and baseline networking of 300 Gbps, this system targets dense compute-heavy workloads. It features AVX-512 vector support but contains no local storage and zero GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached persistence. Benchmark measurements show top-tier results in multi-core stress operations, software compilation, memory throughput, and physics calculations. While CPU-based LLM prompt processing scores in the top tier, token generation runs at average tiers without hardware accelerators. The instance delivers high resource efficiency for scientific computing, physics simulations, batch processing, and clustered HPC clusters.
